contributions.text: Kothden, a test generator for Java that selects inputs by the mutants they kill, targeting surviving mutants.
contributions.quote: First, a generator that targets surviving mutants.

contributions.text: A check that reruns each newly generated test to identify flaky tests, which are reported rather than discarded.
contributions.quote: Second, a check that reruns each new test to find flaky ones.

contributions.text: An evaluation on 30 open-source Java projects, comparing against a random baseline with seeded faults.
contributions.quote: Third, an evaluation on 30 open-source projects.

evaluation.text: The authors report that Kothden found 18 percent more seeded faults than a random baseline at the same ten-minute budget, and that 37 of 42 reported flaky tests were confirmed by hand.
evaluation.quote: Kothden found 18 percent more seeded faults than the baseline.

prior_work.text: The paper contrasts its approach with search-based test generation, which optimizes coverage and does not use mutants, and cites mutation-analysis studies as motivation for using mutants.
prior_work.quote: Search-based test generation [1] optimizes coverage and does not use mutants.

closest_cited_work.text: The genetic algorithm used for input search is described as following the style of earlier search-based unit test generation work.
closest_cited_work.quote: using a genetic algorithm in the style of earlier work [1]
